Fixed by qualifying to 'every same-session phase re-run'.

findings.finding: test_dedup_scan_runs_inside_the_lock only exercised the sessionless unconditional-duplicate branch under the F14 file lock, not the new session-comparison branch, so the concurrency invariant proof did not cover the code path that now decides it.

findings.finding: docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md:3366's session-scoped clause omitted that a matching event with no session of its own still blocks unconditionally, and that an environment with no SHIPWRIGHT_SESSION_ID set never stamps one at all.
findings.suggestion: Add a clause covering both degradations.

findings.finding: test_c3_same_phase_window.py:131-132 and test_completion_writers.py:193-194 assert unconditional 'first-wins' dedup in their docstrings; the premise is now 'first-wins within a session'. Tests still pass since both drive record_event twice under an unchanged env, but the prose is stale.
findings.suggestion: Two-word qualification while the neighbourhood is open.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: A matching phase_completed event with no session of its own can safely, unconditionally block a session-aware caller's write, as the original fix design specified. — has_phase_event returns on the FIRST matching event in scan order, so a single legacy sessionless event for a (phase, splitId) pair permanently re-arms the exact swallowing bug this fix exists to remove, for every later session — and sessionless events are common in practice: convert_configs_to_events.py's migration output, SHIPWRIGHT_SESSION_ID env-var loss in a child shell, and this repo's own shipwright_events.jsonl carries one. Fixed by changing the semantics so a sessionless prior event only blocks a session-blind caller (the historical default); a session-aware caller now proceeds past it, since it cannot be proven to be the same completion. New tests: test_has_phase_event_sessioned_caller_not_blocked_by_sessionless_prior and test_phase_completed_not_deduped_when_prior_event_is_sessionless_via_cli.
findings.suggestion: Narrow the sessionless-blocks rule to only apply to session-blind callers, and prove it with a test that a sessioned caller's write is NOT swallowed by a pre-existing sessionless match.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: All copies of the stale 'record_event dedups phase_completed permanently' claim were corrected by the code-review round. — plugins/shipwright-run/scripts/lib/orchestrator_pkg/events.py:150-158, the phase-end emitter's own contract docstring, carried a 4th, out-of-diff copy ('pairs exactly, as before') that code-review's file list did not cover. Fixed by qualifying it to 'within one SHIPWRIGHT_SESSION_ID' with a pointer to this iterate.
findings.suggestion: Grep the whole repo, not just the files already in the diff, for the exact stale phrase before considering doc-drift closed.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The isinstance(existing_session, str) guard is sufficient on its own; the caller's session value never needs the same guard. — session was checked only for truthiness while existing_session was isinstance-guarded — a non-string truthy session would fail open (compare False against every existing_session, disabling dedup entirely for that call). Not reachable from the CLI today (record_event.py and finalize_iterate.py both source it from os.environ.get, always str), but append_event_idempotent is public API with an existing external caller in shipwright-compliance's _grade_snapshot.py. Fixed by isinstance(session, str)-guarding the caller's session symmetrically before entering the comparison branch.
findings.suggestion: Guard both sides of the comparison identically.
